chunks: What Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He said: I asked him about the taqsir (shortening of prayer). He then said: [It is] for two barids or the whiteness of a day.

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: taqsir: the obligatory shortening of four-rak'ah prayers to two rak'ahs during qualifying travel
key_terms.بَرِيدَيْنِ: two barids: unit of distance; each barid ≈ 4 farsakhs, so two barids ≈ 8 farsakhs (~44 km)
key_terms.بَيَاضِ يَوْمٍ: bayad yawm: 'whiteness of a day', denoting a full day's daytime journey as an alternative expression for the travel threshold

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance for shortening prayer (taqsir) according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the minimum travel distance that obligates taqsir — the shortening of four-rak'ah prayers to two — as two barids (approximately 44 km / 8 farsakhs) or the equivalent of a full day's journey. This criterion is a foundational ruling in Shia fiqh for determining when a traveler must perform qasr prayer.
